score_stage_disabled_because: The best score method (mahalanobis) wrongly rejects 12.2% of BRISC and 27.7% of the genuinely-unseen BRISC subset. Its false rejection RISES as images get less like the training data (12.3% on full BRISC, 27.7% clean-vs-train, 57.8% clean-vs-any), which is the signature of a 'not my training set' detector rather than an out-of-scope detector. A clinic with a different scanner would have most of its scans refused. The precheck's false rejection is flat across the same subsets (0.22%, 0.15%, 0.00%). The threshold above is kept so a human can re-enable this with --enable-score-stage.

color_spread.reason: the image is in colour, and MRI is not

dynamic_range.reason: the image has almost no contrast

frac_dark.reason: the image does not have the dark background a brain scan has

frac_bright.reason: too much of the image is blown out to white

border_mean.reason: the edges of the image are bright, and a brain scan has air at its edges

hist_entropy.reason: the image carries almost no detail

fg_area_frac.reason: no single object of brain-like size was found

fg_centroid_offset.reason: the main object is not near the centre, and a brain slice is centred

fg_border_touch.reason: the main object runs off the edge of the image, and a brain does not

fg_n_components.reason: the image contains many separate objects, and a brain slice has one

notes: Input validation, not deferral. This decides whether the model may judge an image at all. Deferral decides whether a human should double-check an in-scope judgement. Do not merge the two numbers. Entropy and mutual information are in bits (log base 2), matching src/code.py. No threshold here was fitted on BRISC.
